chunks: As for what Humayd ibn al-Ziyad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, or some of our companions, from him, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: 'A man from your mawla died, leaving young children, some property, and a debt, but the creditors do not know about it. If you pay the debt from the value of the children's share, they will have nothing left.' He said: 'Spend it on the children.'

This report has a broken chain, contradicts the apparent meaning of the Quran, while the first two reports are consistent with it, so acting upon them is more appropriate. Allah, the Exalted, said: 'After any bequest he [may have] made or debt [he may have incurred].'
ai.seo_question: How is a deceased person's debt handled if creditors are unaware, according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi evaluates a report from Abu al-Hasan (al-Rida) regarding a deceased man with young children, property, and an undisclosed debt. He rejects the report's implication of paying debts from the heirs' shares, arguing it contradicts the Quranic principle that inheritance distribution occurs only after settling debts and bequests. This establishes the precedence of debt clearance over heir allocation, a foundational rule in Shia fiqh.
